identity: A two-page spread from an Arabic-language school reader (Palestinian curriculum, middle grades): a poetry lesson built on the qasida 'Talawwuth al-Bi'a' by Dr. Mu'taz Ali al-Qutb. It runs: four oral warm-up prompts; the heading al-Nass; the poem; a poet's card (bitaqat al-sha'ir) with name, life and works; then four exercise blocks headed Astaw'ib (comprehension), Unammi Mu'jami (vocabulary), Ufakkir (thinking) and Atadhawwaq (appreciation). It is not running prose but a mosaic of page items: headings, lettered exercise items, table header cells, table body cells, quoted hemistichs and short instruction sentences. The poem was printed in two columns and the linearizer read them as two separate blocks: indices 29-108 are the twelve a'jaz (all rhyming in -la), 110-180 are the twelve asdur, and they pair one-to-one in order (e.g. 'bi-l-amsi qad ghadara l-karbunu madja'ah' at 129-133 pairs with 'min batini l-ardi nahwa l-jawwi muntaqila' at 49-54). The <NL> tokens are physical line breaks of the printed page, so one <NL> span often carries several page items that sat side by side in different columns.
law: The sentence unit here is the PAGE ITEM, not the orthographic clause. A boundary falls at the end of each: (1) heading or section label (al-Nass, Bitaqat al-Sha'ir, Hayatuh, Kitabatuh, Astaw'ib, Unammi Mu'jami, Ufakkir, Atadhawwaq); (2) lettered exercise item, the marker alif/ba/ta/tha always opening its item and never closing the one before; (3) table cell, header or body; (4) quoted hemistich; (5) complete instruction sentence or complete prose sentence. Inside prose, a boundary falls where an independent predication ends and a new one begins WITHOUT a coordinating waw: Arabic chains clauses with waw inside a sentence, so asyndeton between two finite predications is the reliable full-stop signal, and conversely a waw- or thumma-chain is never split. A stem instruction ending in a colon (mimma ya'ti, al-atiya, fi l-jadwal, qala l-sha'ir) closes its own unit and the displayed material after it starts a new one. A run of bare nouns that is the object of such a stem is a comma list, not a run of items, unless the surrounding table proves otherwise. Hemistichs are never split internally, however long, and never merged, however short.
reasoning: PROOF OF THE CELL STRUCTURE, which decides most hard sites. Three independent checks show that a <NL> span routinely concatenates separate cells. (a) 261-277: the values alternate [verse ordinal | prompt] - al-Awwal with 'the places pollution spreads' (verse 1 is 'fi l-barri wa-l-bahri la farqa'), al-Thalith with 'the source of people's anxiety' (verse 3 is 'al-nasu fi qalaqin fa-l-taqsu haddadaha'), al-Khamis with 'two sources of pollution' (verse 5 is 'tilka l-akasidu wa-l-ghazatu qad abithat'). The content matches the verse numbers exactly, so these are paired cells, not prose. I therefore split at 261, 262, 269, 272, 273. (b) 341-405: the four glossary definitions are DELIBERATELY MISMATCHED with their words - nifayat is given the definition of sumum ('substances causing disorders in living things') and sumum the definition of nifayat ('environmental residues... rubbish'). That is the whole point of the matching exercise, and it proves word and definition sit in different columns. Hence splits at 341, 359, 380, 388. Grammar corroborates two of them: 'nifayat al-mawadd allati' and 'sumum mukhallafat al-bi'a' are ungrammatical as single phrases, though al-Akasid and al-Ghazat do read as sentences with their definitions - which is why I hold all four at med rather than hi. (c) 'Raqm al-Bayt' stands alone between <NL>s at 292-293, proving it is a standalone header; so I split it off from al-Matlub at 258. || QUOTED HEMISTICHS ARE THE SAFEST SITES. Where the exercises requote the poem, the same strings already carry given boundaries in the poem body, so the boundary is confirmed, not guessed: 473 wasala (= given at 61), 484 abithat (= given at 139), 594 al-batala (= given at 74), 607 qatibatan (= given at 151), 611 muba'thara (= given at 156), 644 mu'azzama (= given at 121), 661 al-hila (= given at 47). All hi. || EMBEDDED HEADINGS. Three block headings were swallowed mid-line rather than getting their own <NL>: Unammi Mu'jami at 315-316, Ufakkir at 493, Atadhawwaq at 634. Each forces a boundary before it (314 tastaghith, which is also the last table cell 'al-ardu tastaghith'; 492 jadid; 633 basima, the last hemistich of list b) and, for the one-word headings, after it too (493, 634). Compare Astaw'ib at 222, which did get its own line - same kind of object, different luck of layout. The same argument puts a boundary at 211 al-ilmi, since Kitabatuh at 212 is a sub-label parallel to Hayatuh at 192. || THE ALIF PROBLEM AT 228-229. 'Aqra'u l-nassa qira'atan samitatan thumma' then a bare alif then 'akhtaru unwanan badilan'. Ending a sentence on 'thumma' looks wrong, but the item markers ba (250) and ta (279) each open their unit immediately after a <NL>, and ta (528) and tha (533) open theirs mid-line; markers attach forward, never backward. So alif at 229 opens its item and the stem closes at 228, where the printed colon was. Med, because the dangling thumma is unusual. The same rule gives 514 al-jadwal before alif, 527 li-l-talawwuth before ta, 532 al-ard before tha. Note the contrast at 584-585, 'fi qa'imati alif ba' - there the letters are REFERENCES to lists a and b, not markers, so no boundary opens at them; the boundary is at 585, before Qala l-Sha'ir. || THE FOUR TITLE OPTIONS, 238-247. 'Al-ardu tahtadir / al-insanu fi khatar / al-ka'inatu muhaddada / al-insanu yudammiru l-bi'a' are four complete nominal sentences with no connective, the boxed choices for 'choose an alternative title'. Four boundaries, hi. || THE POET BIO, 194-211. 'Min mawalidi madinati l-Qudsi wa-sukkaniha' then, with no waw, 'hasilun ala darajati l-duktura... wa-ya'malu...'. The waw before ya'malu shows the author does chain with waw when he means one sentence; its absence before hasilun is the asyndeton signal. Boundary at 198, med. I do NOT split 'Ismu l-sha'iri Dr Mu'taz Ali al-Qutb' (185-190) or 'Kitabatuhu diwan...' (212-220): each is a well-formed nominal sentence, label as mubtada' and value as khabar, so label-plus-value on one line is one unit. || THE ONE I AM LEAST SURE OF, 420-421. 'Al-bi'a al-taqs al-uzun' after 'the following words'. The proven column structure says three lookup cells; but 141-145 in the poem, 'hamdun sumumun ghubarun kawwanat matara', shows this document does run bare-noun lists together inside one unit. I mark both lo and say plainly that I would not defend them. || 559 al-ard, med: 'fi l-bayti l-tasi'i tawjihatun li-inqadhi l-ard' is a complete statement and 'uhaddiduha' a separate instruction; the item just above it (538-544 statement, 546-552 instruction) prints exactly that pair on two lines, so I read the same pair here with the line break lost. || 679 mujazan, hi: 'Atadhakkaru anna khuruja l-kalimati... yusamma mujazan' then verb-initial 'yastakhdimu l-shu'ara'u...' with no connective - a textbook full stop. Likewise 670 li-l-insan (question ends, boxed note begins) and 639 ujib (instruction ends, quotation begins).
